title: Slatelet prototypes — compact feature sketches
body:
Top-line idea: small, server-powered "slatelets" — highly compact, structured response blobs optimized for mobile/low-bandwidth clients and ephemeral display surfaces. Think: tiny, self-contained render recipes that survive intermittent connectivity, cost less to produce, and are easy to cache on-device.

Why: we keep getting requests from mobile product folks and partners for faster perceived responsiveness and predictable token cost on low-latency surfaces. Full-text completions or long chat histories are heavy; a tiny, pre-renderable payload with multiple fidelity layers could unlock snappy UX and less wasted token spend.

Key constraints / design goals:
- <= 1 KB canonical payload for baseline fidelity (aim for 800–1000 bytes).
- Predictable cost: bounded token generation budget per slatelet.
- Multi-fidelity: small/medium/expanded variants (tiny summary -> short bullets -> 1-paragraph).
- Render agnostic: JSON recipe + optional pre-rendered HTML fallback. Mobile app/SDK does minimal interpretation.
- Cacheable and TTL-aware: server includes a TTL and version fingerprint for local cache/invalidations.
- Privacy-friendly: no raw user transcripts embedded; only necessary metadata.

User stories (quick):
- As a mobile user, I want search results to show an instant one-line answer while the full assistant wakes up.
- As an app engineer, I want to cache responses for repeat queries and avoid hitting the model for frequent ephemeral prompts.
- As a product manager, I want to measure perceived latency (time-to-first-slatelet) and reduce median token cost by 30% for targeted flows.

Slatelet shape (first stab):
- id: string (fingerprint)
- version: semver
- fidelity: enum[thumbnail, brief, expanded]
- tokens_budget: int (approx)
- ttl_seconds: int
- render: { type: enum[json_recipe, html_snippet, markdown], payload: string }  <-- note: this will be stored as stringified fragment to keep payload shape small
- meta: [tags], safety_flags: [low|mod], cache_hint: [stale-while-revalidate seconds]
- actions: optional list of action templates (deep-link identifiers)

Implementation notes / server behavior:
- Generation path: lite-model (e.g., 2-4B quantized) for thumbnail/brief. Fall back to a higher-capacity model only for expanded.
- Adaptive budget: if the user is on high-SLA route (paid customer), allow medium fidelity by default.
- Dedup/canonicalization: generate canonical key based on normalized prompt + schema; reuse existing slatelets where possible.
- Prefetching hint: on query patterns (search -> detail), pre-create brief slatelets for likely follow-ups.
- Storage: small object store (S3 or KV) keyed by id with metadata in DB for TTL and versioning.

API sketch (hosted):
- POST /v1/slatelets/generate -> returns id + payload (if immediate) + fingerprint
- GET /v1/slatelets/{id} -> fetch by id (fast path)
- POST /v1/slatelets/query-cache -> returns cached id or trigger generation (useful for client-side optimistic read)
- Optional streaming: initial thumbnail then stream brief/expanded as they become ready

Client SDK UX notes:
- Provide a SlateletView component for mobile SDKs that accepts id or prompt. If id, it fetches and renders; if prompt, it hits /generate and shows thumbnail immediately.
- Local caching: store id -> payload with TTL. Expose on-device invalidation API and listener hooks.

Metrics to track (minimum):
- time_to_first_slatelet (client perceived)
- token_cost_per_interaction (median by fidelity)
- cache_hit_rate (client + server)
- fallbacks_to_full_completion (how often slot expanded into heavy completion)
- user_engagement_delta (CTR on actions from slatelet vs baseline)

Rollout plan (conceptual):
1) internal sandbox for low-risk flows (docs search, FAQ answers). 2) small customer pilot (two mobile customers) with A/B comparing slatelet-first vs full completion. 3) expand to other surfaces after safety/metrics OK.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- API supports thumbnail + brief fidelity and returns <= 1 KB for thumbnail in 90th percentile.
- SDK renders slatelet within 150ms median from app request (including network).
- Token spend per interaction reduced by >=25% on targeted flows.
- No new safety incidents in pilot (human review sampling).

Open questions / risks:
- Safety: compressing content down may obscure context needed for safe responses. Need guardrails/explicit flags that escalate to full model when uncertain.
- Caching semantics: what if cached slatelet becomes stale and misleads users? TTLs and stale-while-revalidate needed.
- Cost model: storing many tiny objects could increase storage overhead; need lifecycle policies and eviction.
- Internationalization: how to support language-specific brevity and token budgets.
- UI fragmentation: too many fidelity variants may complicate client implementation. Start with two: thumbnail + brief.

Prototype experiment ideas (week 1–2):
- Hack: wire up search FAQ index -> generate slatelets for top N queries and show in internal mobile app. Measure time-to-first-meaningful-paint.
- Simulate cache hits by pre-seeding client with slatelets for common queries and measure token savings.
- Instrument fallback triggers: random 5% of slatelet responses expand to full completion to check quality.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to Leo about on-device cache format and size limits (esp iOS).
- Ask Mika about lightweight safety checks we can run cheaply (classifier micro-model?).
- Draft a one-pager for growth with example mockups for mobile and web.
- Add a quick cost model: compute storage vs token savings for 1M queries/month.

Rough session backlog / milestones:
- Week 1: API prototype + simple JSON recipe shape. Internal demo.
- Week 2: iOS/Android SDK wrappers + basic rendering component.
- Week 3: Pilot with FAQ dataset + metrics instrumentation.
- Week 4–6: Safety sampling + performance tuning + pilot evaluation.

Quick mock UX prompts (for designers/devs):
- Thumbnail: one-sentence summary + icon + action chevron.
- Brief: 3 bullet points with tappable deep-links.
- Expanded: paragraph + sources + optional inline tool buttons.

Last thought: slatelets feel like a middle-layer between embeddings-based retrieval snippets and full chat completions. If we design them right they could be used across product surfaces (search, notifications, onboarding tooltips) and also be a building block for low-cost fallbacks in Dedicated/Private deployments. Prioritize cacheability and deterministic small size.
